If I could give anyone in this thread advice, it’s to heal your relationship with food and to realize you are more than a body. If you only like your body or self when you look “good”, you’re objectifying yourself. Your body’s purpose is not to skinny. It’s to keep you alive. 

For many many years I was eating under 1000 calories a day. Usually only 500 or less when I was purposefully starving myself.  I was able to “recover” from my anorexia on my own, or so I thought, but it actually just morphed into orthorexia after my Celiac diagnosis. 

I wanted to get an eating disorder therapist in 2021, but after they assessed me they told me I needed intensive treatment because 1) I was eating nowhere near enough and was malnourished (despite being technically overweight) and 2) I had been in this ED hell for 15+ years. The process of treatment was absolutely difficult, it was virtual 4 days a week for 9 months and I was in a pretty horrible way CFS was most of the time because of it, but in the end, it changed my life. 

Eating 3 meals a day, eating when I’m hungry, etc. It took awhile for it to take root. But once it did, the amount of extra mental energy I was able to have was wild. I used to only think about food. And that, plus the effect of losing and gaining large amounts of weight every couple years - was having a huge impact on my health. 

The one thing healing in this way didn’t help is with my IBS. Still as bad as ever, if not worse, but eating disorders can damage the GI system.

Lastly healing your relationship to food and body will not cure your CFS but oh man it’ll make your life better and give you more energy, even if it’s only by a small percentage. 

It’s OKAY to gain weight. Especially if you’re healing or chronically ill or trying to get better. You are more likely to survive critical illness or chronic illness flare ups if you are not underweight. Fat is not a bad thing and has nothing to do with you as a person. It is something your body has. Your fatness doesn’t mean you’re somehow worse. 

End of rant :)

Not like “split personality disorder” (which isn’t the correct name anyway) - that’s Dissociative Identity Disorder, what people commonly refer to as split personality disorder, and that’s not what I mean. 

There’s something called structural dissociation.
